messages.author: edbb58ff07e2feec
messages.subject: differential bundle functioning with empirical_ES
parts:
Hi Phil,


Thanks for your recent help and apologies for multiple posts. I am now trying DBF (on a literacy assessment using passages/tasks as the "bundle") and am using the recent Psychometrika article as a guide. I am assuming that the DRF stats referred to in the article are those produced in empirical_ES, but please correct me if otherwise!


As far as DBF goes.... If I don't have an entire bundle of items that aren't "suspicious", can I use a set of individual anchor items? Let's say I used the "drop" method and found these individual items to be invariant: 4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37. 


I set up the anchor model for two of my groups as:


model_anchor1.3<- multipleGroup(DIF1and3items, model = Q1, group = group1.3,
                              invariance = c(itemnames[c(4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37)], 
                                             'free_means', 'free_var'))

followed by:

empirical_ES(model_anchor1.3, Theta.focal = NULL, focal_items = c(1:3,5, 40), 
                             DIF = F, ref.group = 1, plot = F)

          Effect Size       Value
1                STDS  0.02569611
2                UTDS  0.10028021
3              UETSDS  0.05264130
4               ETSSD  0.04032799
5         Starks.DTFR  0.02194441
6               UDTFR  0.10159374
7              UETSDN  0.05257948
8 theta.of.max.test.D -2.34820862
9           Test.Dmax -0.14124992

(also please see attached plot) 


Question 1. Is it ok that item 4, which was identified as an anchor item, is omitted from this DBF, even though it is technically in the first bundle? So basically my bundles "work around" the anchor items, even if they are part of the bundle. 

Question 2. Does  empirical_ES use the original anchor items from the model_anchor1.3?

Question 3. I am wondering about nested testing for DBF. For DIF for the first passage (same as above), but with all six of my groups (I know.... 6 groups....yikes), I ran:

P1_items1_metric <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_metric

P1_items1_scalar <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1', 'd'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_scalar

P1_items1_difficulty <- DIF(model_anchor, c('d'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_difficulty 

Output looks something like this:

> P1_items1_difficulty
$rmc01
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850351 1850394 1854351 1856840 -924392.7    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 21.582   5 0.001

$rmc02
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850342 1850385 1854342 1856831 -924388.0    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 12.291   5 0.031

etc.

Is there a way to get these stats at the bundle level? I tried anova (x,y) but I guess anova doesn't work with DIF. Perhaps I could run MultipleGroup model with CONSTRAINB to model DBF but I am not sure what that would look like. Although perhaps the empirical_ES is sufficient in terms of reporting? Sorry, getting a bit turned around here. Thank you in advance for any advice you could offer! 

Jeanne

On Tue, Jun 26, 2018 at 9:46 AM Jeanne Sinclair <jeanneh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil,


Thanks for your recent help and apologies for multiple posts. I am now trying DBF (on a literacy assessment using passages/tasks as the "bundle") and am using the recent Psychometrika article as a guide. I am assuming that the DRF stats referred to in the article are those produced in empirical_ES, but please correct me if otherwise!

They are not, sadly. Though I talk briefly about the emperical_ES statistics as approximation of the DRF statistics of varying degrees (all of which are suboptimal in comparison, to differing degrees). The DRF() function is the go-to for obtaining these statistics.

As far as DBF goes.... If I don't have an entire bundle of items that aren't "suspicious", can I use a set of individual anchor items? Let's say I used the "drop" method and found these individual items to be invariant: 4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37. 


I set up the anchor model for two of my groups as:


model_anchor1.3<- multipleGroup(DIF1and3items, model = Q1, group = group1.3,
                              invariance = c(itemnames[c(4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37)], 
                                             'free_means', 'free_var'))

followed by:

empirical_ES(model_anchor1.3, Theta.focal = NULL, focal_items = c(1:3,5, 40), 
                             DIF = F, ref.group = 1, plot = F)

          Effect Size       Value
1                STDS  0.02569611
2                UTDS  0.10028021
3              UETSDS  0.05264130
4               ETSSD  0.04032799
5         Starks.DTFR  0.02194441
6               UDTFR  0.10159374
7              UETSDN  0.05257948
8 theta.of.max.test.D -2.34820862
9           Test.Dmax -0.14124992

(also please see attached plot) 


Question 1. Is it ok that item 4, which was identified as an anchor item, is omitted from this DBF, even though it is technically in the first bundle? So basically my bundles "work around" the anchor items, even if they are part of the bundle.
Yes, that's fine and indeed appropriate. Anchor items should contribute 0 to the effect size magnitude in DBF bundles because the response curves across groups are identical.
Question 2. Does  empirical_ES use the original anchor items from the model_anchor1.3?
Yes.

Question 3. I am wondering about nested testing for DBF. For DIF for the first passage (same as above), but with all six of my groups (I know.... 6 groups....yikes), I ran:

P1_items1_metric <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_metric

P1_items1_scalar <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1', 'd'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_scalar

P1_items1_difficulty <- DIF(model_anchor, c('d'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_difficulty 

Output looks something like this:

> P1_items1_difficulty
$rmc01
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850351 1850394 1854351 1856840 -924392.7    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 21.582   5 0.001

$rmc02
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850342 1850385 1854342 1856831 -924388.0    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 12.291   5 0.031

etc.

Is there a way to get these stats at the bundle level? I tried anova (x,y) but I guess anova doesn't work with DIF. Perhaps I could run MultipleGroup model with CONSTRAINB to model DBF but I am not sure what that would look like. Although perhaps the empirical_ES is sufficient in terms of reporting? Sorry, getting a bit turned around here. Thank you in advance for any advice you could offer!

This approach identifies items with DIF, and are basically more flexible models than the constrained one. If you want to be testing for DBF you have to allow for the effects of DIF for each suspicious item in the same fitted model, and after that has been fitted test whether the aggregate effects of the DIF items results in an overall bundle bias effect. So, given this information, you would need to fit a new, more flexible model first, and then use the DRF()/empirical_ES() functions to test for DBF. HTH.
 

Jeanne

Thank you!

On Tuesday, June 26, 2018 at 12:39:32 PM UTC-4, Phil Chalmers wrote:

On Tue, Jun 26, 2018 at 9:46 AM Jeanne Sinclair <jeanneh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil,


Thanks for your recent help and apologies for multiple posts. I am now trying DBF (on a literacy assessment using passages/tasks as the "bundle") and am using the recent Psychometrika article as a guide. I am assuming that the DRF stats referred to in the article are those produced in empirical_ES, but please correct me if otherwise!


They are not, sadly. Though I talk briefly about the emperical_ES statistics as approximation of the DRF statistics of varying degrees (all of which are suboptimal in comparison, to differing degrees). The DRF() function is the go-to for obtaining these statistics.  


As far as DBF goes.... If I don't have an entire bundle of items that aren't "suspicious", can I use a set of individual anchor items? Let's say I used the "drop" method and found these individual items to be invariant: 4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37. 


I set up the anchor model for two of my groups as:


model_anchor1.3<- multipleGroup(DIF1and3items, model = Q1, group = group1.3,
                              invariance = c(itemnames[c(4, 6, 7, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 25, 34, 37)], 
                                             'free_means', 'free_var'))

followed by:

empirical_ES(model_anchor1.3, Theta.focal = NULL, focal_items = c(1:3,5, 40), 
                             DIF = F, ref.group = 1, plot = F)

          Effect Size       Value
1                STDS  0.02569611
2                UTDS  0.10028021
3              UETSDS  0.05264130
4               ETSSD  0.04032799
5         Starks.DTFR  0.02194441
6               UDTFR  0.10159374
7              UETSDN  0.05257948
8 theta.of.max.test.D -2.34820862
9           Test.Dmax -0.14124992

(also please see attached plot) 


Question 1. Is it ok that item 4, which was identified as an anchor item, is omitted from this DBF, even though it is technically in the first bundle? So basically my bundles "work around" the anchor items, even if they are part of the bundle. 

Yes, that's fine and indeed appropriate. Anchor items should contribute 0 to the effect size magnitude in DBF bundles because the response curves across groups are identical. 
 

Question 2. Does  empirical_ES use the original anchor items from the model_anchor1.3?

Yes. 
 

Question 3. I am wondering about nested testing for DBF. For DIF for the first passage (same as above), but with all six of my groups (I know.... 6 groups....yikes), I ran:

P1_items1_metric <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_metric

P1_items1_scalar <- DIF(model_anchor, c('a1', 'd'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_scalar

P1_items1_difficulty <- DIF(model_anchor, c('d'), items2test = c(1:3,5)) #binary items
P1_items1_difficulty 

Output looks something like this:

> P1_items1_difficulty
$rmc01
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850351 1850394 1854351 1856840 -924392.7    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 21.582   5 0.001

$rmc02
      AIC    AICc   SABIC     BIC    logLik     X2  df     p
1 1850342 1850385 1854342 1856831 -924388.0    NaN NaN   NaN
2 1850340 1850383 1854365 1856870 -924381.9 12.291   5 0.031

etc.

Is there a way to get these stats at the bundle level? I tried anova (x,y) but I guess anova doesn't work with DIF. Perhaps I could run MultipleGroup model with CONSTRAINB to model DBF but I am not sure what that would look like. Although perhaps the empirical_ES is sufficient in terms of reporting? Sorry, getting a bit turned around here. Thank you in advance for any advice you could offer! 

This approach identifies items with DIF, and are basically more flexible models than the constrained one. If you want to be testing for DBF you have to allow for the effects of DIF for each suspicious item in the same fitted model, and after that has been fitted test whether the aggregate effects of the DIF items results in an overall bundle bias effect. So, given this information, you would need to fit a new, more flexible model first, and then use the DRF()/empirical_ES() functions to test for DBF. HTH.
 

Jeanne

Question 1. Is it ok that item 4, which was identified as an anchor item, is omitted from this DBF, even though it is technically in the first bundle? So basically my bundles "work around" the anchor items, even if they are part of the bundle. 

Yes, that's fine and indeed appropriate. Anchor items should contribute 0 to the effect size magnitude in DBF bundles because the response curves across groups are identical. 
 

Question 2. Does  empirical_ES use the original anchor items from the model_anchor1.3?

This approach identifies items with DIF, and are basically more flexible models than the constrained one. If you want to be testing for DBF you have to allow for the effects of DIF for each suspicious item in the same fitted model, and after that has been fitted test whether the aggregate effects of the DIF items results in an overall bundle bias effect. So, given this information, you would need to fit a new, more flexible model first, and then use the DRF()/empirical_ES() functions to test for DBF. HTH.
